reasons: The cited termination provisions (p0118, p0128-p0129, p0131) only run one way — Sparkling must cease use and return/destroy Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes — and contain no obligation on Garman to return Sparkling's data or provide exit help, so 'missing' is the correct status and the rule's fallback (90 days assistance plus 30-day export) is genuinely unmet.

The inserted Section 17(d) tracks the model language closely and reaches the preferred position with a single additive paragraph placed in the termination section (after the last 17(c) text), which is the smallest edit that achieves the playbook outcome; no existing wording is disturbed.

All three required elements are present and correctly directed at the Vendor (Garman): up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days, and subsequent deletion with written certification.
The comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required prefix, explains what changed and why, and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing.

Survival is adequately covered by p0131's 'require or contemplate performance after termination ... include but are not limited to' language, so omitting 17(d) from the enumerated list is not a defect; deterministic checks also pass.
